data.exact_reserve_text: For the 2015 underwriting year, the current estimate of cumulative gross claims is GBP 549k, compared to the estimate of GBP 539k at 24 months, indicating a strengthening of GBP 10k. The report also states: 'In 2017, there has been an overall surplus in ultimate claims of GBP 0.2m (2016: GBP 0.7m) due primarily to a reduction in claims estimates as uncertainty around catastrophe exposure unwinds.'

data.standardized_narrative: Syndicate 6103 reported a gross strengthening of GBP 0.01 million (1.37% of opening gross reserves) for prior year reserves, specifically for the 2015 underwriting year. This contrasts with a narrative statement of an overall net surplus of GBP 0.2 million in ultimate claims for 2017, attributed to a reduction in claims estimates and unwinding catastrophe exposure uncertainty. The syndicate had no material exposure to Hurricanes Harvey, Irma, or Maria for the 2015 or 2016 years of account, but Hurricane Matthew in 2016 elevated the incurred loss ratio for that year.
data.data_quality_notes: Prior year development is calculated from the gross claims development triangle for the 2015 underwriting year, showing a strengthening of GBP 0.01m. This contradicts the narrative on page 27 which states an overall net surplus of GBP 0.2m in ultimate claims for 2017, attributed to a reduction in claims estimates and unwinding catastrophe exposure uncertainty. The causes provided in the report relate to this net surplus, not the gross strengthening. Syndicate 6103 reinsured to close all liabilities on 2014 and prior underwriting years, so only the 2015 year of account is considered for prior year development.
